newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN fears possible outbreak of epidemics in Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: UN fears possible outbreak of epidemics in Rwanda.

text.p: The U.N. health agency said on Tuesday that it feared epidemics could break out among the weakest in the flood of Hutu refugees returning to Rwanda and said cholera, which has been confirmed, remained a big risk.

"The health situation is grave. These people are hungry and exhausted, they haven't had food and good water for a long time. This is ideal ground for explosion of diseases -- malaria, diarrhoea, infections," Ebrahim Samba, head of Africa division at the World Health Organisation (WHO) told a Geneva briefing.

In one of the biggest homeward refugee movements in recent history which caught aid agencies off-guard, half a million Rwandan Hutus poured out of east Zaire's Goma region after Tutsi rebels shelled a camp and forced Hutu militiamen to flee.

WHO said two cases of cholera had been reported on Sunday at the hospital in Rwanda's northwestern border town of Gisenyi, the entry point for the refugees. There were confirmed cases of cholera also in Goma town across the border, it said.

"Cholera is there. It's been confirmed and the potential for it to spread through Rwanda is very big," David Heymann, another WHO specialist, told the briefing. "For every one case visible, there could be a hundred other cases that are not visible."

A cholera outbreak claimed more than 30,000 lives in 1994 in Goma when Rwandan Hutu refugees fled after a Hutu-led genocide of minority Tutsis. At the peak of the epidemic, more than 5,000 people died in a single day.
